A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReLN research, with matching authors, core construction, and retained experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReLN experiments on algebraic benchmarks, jet tagging, and simulated drone trajectory estimation, including comparisons and input ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Gaussian-splat learning, double-pendulum experiments, additional baselines, and component ablations.

M1.justification: The core bilinear form and ReLN layer rules remain unchanged. However, Section 5.3 and Appendix K introduce a substantial Gaussian-MAE adaptation with ReLN encoding/decoding, scalar-conditioned attention, central positional embeddings, and replacement of the classification token with global pooling. The reported jet-tagging message equation also adds the second particle's self-contraction.

E1.justification: v2 adds ShapeSplat/ShapeNet Gaussian reconstruction pretraining, aligned and rotated ModelNet10 classification, and double-spring-pendulum Hamiltonian dynamics under O(2), SO(2), and D6. These introduce new data representations, tasks, and physical scenarios. The original algebraic, jet-tagging, and drone coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The drone comparison adds Tensor Field Networks, SE(3)-Transformer, and Lie Neurons, including covariance variants. The jet-tagging comparison adds CGENN and reproduced Lie Neurons results. Gaussian-MAE, EMLP-HNN, and MLP-HNN become comparators in the new experiments; these are actual reported comparisons, not citation additions alone.

E3.justification: New protocols include masked Gaussian reconstruction followed by classification fine-tuning, and pendulum training on a 500/500/500 split with 30-second rollout evaluation and computational measurements. Jet tagging adds a 224k-parameter ReLN configuration. Appendix I.5 also reverses the stated VN sign-fixing and handedness-enforcement order relative to v1; this is a reported preprocessing revision, without evidence that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted drone ablations removing the central or semisimple contribution, directly testing the proposed reductive construction (Tables 3 and 13). It also adds Gaussian rotation-robustness tests, reconstruction convergence curves (Figure 8), and expanded trajectory case studies with additional baselines (Figure 7). v1's velocity/covariance/log-covariance analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Table 5 and Appendix L newly specify three independent random-seed trials and standard deviations for the pendulum results. Existing five-run classification reporting and jet-tagging uncertainty reporting are retained. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: The original algebraic, drone, and 84k jet-tagging scores are retained. New results include ModelNet10 accuracies of 94.82% aligned and 95.15% rotated for ReLN versus 93.39% and 18.28% for Gaussian-MAE, pendulum errors and computational costs, and additional drone baselines/ablations. Table 11 adds a 224k ReLN rejection score of 2201±101; this is a new configuration, while the 84k result remains 1979±87.

T1.justification: Appendix F introduces theoretical scaling under a fixed scalar-feature budget, deriving linear-layer cost C²/n² and bracket cost O(Cn), with a layerwise comparison. Appendix B adds explicit classical gl(n) Killing-form identities and a proof intertwining SO(3) vector and adjoint actions. The principal nondegeneracy, logarithmic-map, and output-equivariance proofs are retained under reorganized numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand to Gaussian-splat representation learning and multi-symmetry Hamiltonian dynamics, making accuracy and parameter/compute efficiency central claims. The introduction now characterizes algebraic and jet-tagging performance as matching baselines, moderating earlier superiority language. Exact adjoint equivariance remains the central architectural claim.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly distinguishes covariance congruence from GL(n) adjoint action, limiting their equivalence to orthogonal frame changes and identifying translation-related extensions. The unchanged sp(4) results no longer motivate superior numerical conditioning, and Appendix H.1 interprets jet-tagging differences more cautiously. New drone interpretations address reductive-component contributions and convolution versus attention.

D1.justification: Appendices K–L document Gaussian sampling, masking, optimizer schedules, pretraining/fine-tuning budgets, pendulum generation and model settings, and JAX HLO FLOP measurement. Appendix I adds tensor-baseline feature decomposition and temporal-graph construction, plus explicit relative-translation-error windows and stride. These substantially expand implementation information; newly disclosed details do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive positioning against Gaussian-splat learning methods and Clifford/geometric-algebra architectures, including Ma, Lu, Zhang, Ye, Brehmer, Liu, and Filimoshina. It argues that coupled geometric attributes distinguish ReLN from Gaussian-learning approaches. Several earlier citations, including Battiloro, Eschmann, and Yu, are removed, while the central relationship to Lie Neurons and Vector Neurons is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and experimental interpretations are extensively rewritten. Jet tagging moves from the main experiments to Appendix H, a separate limitations section is introduced, and the theoretical appendices are reorganized. Layer explanations and notation are clarified, including removal of the duplicated ReLN-ReLU bullet.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Gaussian-MAE architecture diagram, reconstruction-learning curves, expanded trajectory plots, and Gaussian, pendulum, and complexity tables. The drone results are redesigned into a compact main table and fuller appendix table. The original group survey is expanded and relocated, jet-tagging displays move to the appendix, and Figure 4's case selection and caption change.

improvement.justification: v1's uncertainty-processing evidence lacked tensor-based comparators and targeted tests of the reductive components. v2 addresses both weaknesses through TFN/SE(3)-Transformer comparisons and component ablations, while Section 6 clarifies an important equivariance boundary. Additional applications and implementation details substantially strengthen support and assessability. These gains outweigh remaining overclaims: Table 6 supports lower FLOPs and latency but reports more ReLN-HNN parameters than EMLP-HNN, and Section 5.3 still overstates GL(3) equivariance relative to the stated covariance limitation.
